leads.title: Alabama Senate Bill 320 - repeal of sodomy / deviate sexual intercourse ban
leads.documents: Legal status of same-sex sexual activity in Alabama; repeal of unenforceable sodomy ban after Lawrence v. Texas.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: House passed May 23, 2019 with 101 yes and 3 absent; Senate passed May 28, 2019 with 32 yea and 3 absent; effective September 1, 2019. Linked in text to Lawrence v. Texas (2003) striking down state sodomy laws.

leads.title: Obergefell v. Hodges (U.S. Supreme Court, June 26, 2015) with Alabama marriage bans
leads.documents: Nationwide same-sex marriage legality vs Alabama resistance and enforcement machinery; unenforceable state bans.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: June 26, 2015 ruling; by 2017 eight counties refusing any licenses; May 2019 Legislature required recording marriage certificates; Aug 29, 2019 all counties recording for all couples. Unenforceable prohibitions listed as Executive Order Number 24 by Gov. Fob James (1996), statute 1998, Alabama Code Sec. 30-1-19, constitutional amendment June 2006 / Amendment 774.

leads.title: Alabama Vulnerable Child Compassion and Protection Act (SB 184)
leads.documents: Criminal ban on gender-affirming care for minors - core trans legal risk and enforcement penalty.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: Passed early 2022, signed April 8 by Gov. Kay Ivey, effective May 8, 2022; Class C felony for provider giving puberty blockers, hormones, surgeries to anyone under 19, punishable by 10 years prison; 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals Aug 21, 2023 allowed enforcement pending permanent decision; trial scheduled April 2, 2024. State hired expert James Cantor; Judge Liles C. Burke gave testimony very little weight.

leads.title: Boe v. Marshall aka Eknes-Tucker v. Ivey
leads.documents: Court challenge to gender-affirming care ban by five parents; scope of parental rights, DOJ involvement, current enforceability.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: Five parents sued with AG Steve Marshall defendant; state sought all medical/mental health records on gender dysphoria; Judge Burke May 13, 2022 temporarily halted puberty blocker/hormone ban but left surgery ban; summarized in The New York Times as sex discrimination / parental rights issue; Aug 2023 three-judge 11th Circuit panel allowed ban; Sept 11, 2023 rehearing request; Dec 26, 2023 Judge Burke allowed case to continue; Jan 2023 expense review >$1M legal counsel + >$500K experts; plaintiffs withdrew May 1, 2025, ban remained in force.

leads.title: Corbitt v. Taylor
leads.documents: Identity-document rules for trans people; surgical procedure + name-change requirement to amend birth certificate / driver's license sex marker.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: Alabama allows amendment with documentation of sex changed by surgical procedure and name change; Jan 2021 federal judge ruled surgery requirement violated plaintiff's rights in part under Equal Protection Clause; appealed a month later to Eleventh Circuit by defendants; Eleventh Circuit struck down lower ruling, leaving requirement standing.

leads.title: Alabama HB322 / Act No. 2022-290
leads.documents: Public-school bathroom ban tied to birth certificate and K-5 classroom instruction ban on sexuality/gender; Board of Education codification.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: Passed House Feb 2022 and Senate April 2022 with amendment banning K-5 instruction on sexuality and gender; signed April 8, 2022 by Gov. Ivey as Act No. 2022-290; implemented/codified in full Sept 2022 by Alabama Board of Education; March 2024 House/Senate bill to eliminate DEI and ban university bathroom use misaligned with sex assigned at birth.

leads.title: Alabama Senate Bill 79 (2025)
leads.documents: State-level legal definition of gender as immutable male-female binary and authorization of separate single-sex spaces.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: Signed Feb 2025 by Gov. Kay Ivey; declares gender immutable binary determined by biological sex assigned at birth; neither state nor political subdivision shall be prohibited from establishing separate single-sex spaces when biology, privacy, safety, or fairness implicated.

leads.title: Alabama House Bill 261 (2023) and 2021 K-12 sports law
leads.documents: Trans sports exclusion in public schools and colleges/universities based on biological / assigned-at-birth sex.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: Since July 1, 2021 single-sex public school teams must consider biological sex, signed by Gov. Ivey; HB261 signed May 30, 2023 prohibits college/university competition on team differing from sex assigned at birth even with gender-affirming hormone therapy, except co-ed sports.

leads.title: Alabama hate-crime statute and Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act
leads.documents: Lack of state hate-crime protection for sexual orientation/gender identity vs federal coverage; legislative attempts to add protections.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: Since 1994 Alabama law covers race, color, religion, national origin, ethnicity, physical/mental disability only; Rep. Alvin Holmes HB533 April 24, 2009 to add sexual orientation (Rep. Patricia Todd sought gender identity), House passed 46-41, Senate Judiciary approved but full Senate no action before May 15, 2009 adjournment; prior bills HB829 (2008), HB247 (2007), HB57 (2006), HB423 (2001), HB85 (2000); HB413 (2016), HB8 (2017) failed; 2019 police-officer bill with Sen. Vivian Davis Figures amendment for sexual orientation passed committee but not legislature; federal Act approved by Congress signed by President Barack Obama Oct 2009 bans such hate crimes federally.

leads.title: Public Religion Research Institute (PRRI) polls + The New York Times feature + Movement Advancement Project / Equaldex profiles
leads.documents: Institutional/human-rights context and public-opinion environment for LGBTQ people in Alabama; anti-discrimination support and religious-refusal attitudes.
leads.detail: No URLs visible except via labels. Citation detail visible: PRRI 2017 - 42% support same-sex marriage vs 51% oppose, 58% support anti-discrimination law; PRRI 2022 - 53% support marriage vs 41% oppose, 69% support anti-discrimination; 2025 - 54% support marriage, 66% support anti-discrimination, 50% oppose religious refusals. Further reading: Polgreen, L.; Williams, D.L. (Jan 6, 2023), Want to Understand L.G.B.T.Q. Life in America? Go to Alabama., The New York Times, retrieved Jan 7, 2023. External links listed: LGBT Rights in Alabama - via Equaldex; Alabama's Equality Profile - via Movement Advancement Project.
